# Image Milnor numbers

!!! info "Where this comes from"
    Image Milnor numbers are consequences of the [S₀ series](@MD@/singularities/multi/empty.md) of the empty multi-singularity.

<div class="wp-content" markdown="0">
<strong>Image Milnor numbers for quasihomogeneous germs </strong>

The image Milnor number \(\mu_I(f)\) of a (finite) quasihomogeneous germ \(f:(C^m,0) \to (C^{m+1},0)\) with \(m \leq 14\) is determined by its weights \((W_1,\ldots,W_m)\) and degrees \((D_1,\ldots,D_{m+1})\). In this website we present how the weights and degrees determine the image Milnor number, following  

[KR] J. Koncki, R. Rim&aacute;nyi: <a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.14602">Higher characteristic classes of multisingularity loci</a>, Section 9. 

This work builds on 
[Oh] T. Ohmoto. <a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/1309.0661">Singularities of maps and characteristic classes</a>. In School on Real and Complex Singularities in S&atilde;o Carlos, 2012, number 68 in Adv. Studies in Pure Math., pages 191-265, 2016, Section 6, and
[PPS] I. Pallar&eacute;s and G. Pe&ntilde;afort-Sanchis: <a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/1810.09002">Image Milnor number formulas for weighted-homogeneous map-germs</a>. Results Math., 76(3): Paper No. 152, 23, 2021.<hr>We present the result in three different ways:

<strong> 1 </strong>: [the most economic way] One (reasonable size) polynomial determines the formulas for all m.
 
<strong> 2 </strong>: [medium way] A list of 15 polynomials (K-polynomials) determine the 15 formulas, recursively.
